message.content:
The “best” month to visit Hawaii really depends on what you’re looking for—weather, crowds, or price. Here’s a quick rundown:

| Goal | Ideal Months | Why |
|------|--------------|-----|
| **Lowest crowds & good weather** | **April–May** (spring) and **September–October** (early fall) | These shoulder seasons have warm, sunny weather but fewer tourists than the peak summer months. |
| **Best overall experience** | **May–June** or **September–October** | Warm temperatures, plenty of sunshine, and still relatively mild crowds. |
| **Lowest prices** | **January–March** and **November–December** | Off‑peak season means cheaper flights and accommodations, though it can be a bit cooler and more rainy. |
| **Surfing & water sports** | **June–August** | The trade winds are strongest, creating ideal surf conditions on the leeward side. |
| **Hiking & outdoor activities** | **April–June** and **September–October** | Warm days and cooler evenings make for comfortable hiking conditions. |

If you’re flexible, aim for the shoulder seasons (late spring or early fall). That’s when you’ll get a great mix of warm weather, fewer crowds, and better deals.
